messages:
maria: ping 0:12 customer reported a failed rewrap during a DR switch. They used BYOK import and we returned a 403 on the rewrap call.
lucas: can you drop the proxy error + req id?
maria: log snippet:
```
2026-04-02T10:11:02Z WARN hsm-proxy rewrap req=zz9 region=us-central1 code=403 msg=\"forbidden: attestation mismatch\" fingerprint=sha256:AA11BB22
```
ash: that fingerprint is different from the one on record for the tenant? if so proxy rightly blocked it.
ops-oncall: I ran a quick audit: tenant record shows fingerprint sha256:CC33DD44. There was a short maintenance window at 10:00 that touched the HSM proxy cluster.
maria: customer wants to know: (1) who is responsible for the failed rotation, (2) what evidence we can hand them for regulators, (3) whether we will change RBAC to avoid this in future.
lucas: responsibility depends on custody mode. If they chose retain-custody (their HSM holds master key) and they rotated operator keys or reinitialized shards without updating attestation, the rotation would fail due to mismatched fingerprint -> ops on customer. If we had a proxy bug that rewrote expected fingerprint during maintenance, that's on us.
qa: request: include chain-of-custody timeline (import, attestations, rewrap attempts), proxy verification result, and any RBAC grants used. Need to be machine-friendly for compliance.
security-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-2026-0402-BYOK-REWRAP (sev: medium). Runbook: security/runbooks/byok-rewrap
ops-oncall: Proposed evidence package contents:
- import transaction record (txn id, timestamp, operator id)
- attestation blob (base64) + attestation verification result
- proxy verification log for req zz9 (redact internal hostnames/IPs)
- KMS-backend rewrap attempt trace (if any)
- RBAC audit lines showing which principals called custody:rotate
- timeline CSV (iso timestamps)
lucas: For audit retention, customer asked for 18 months. We currently retain 12 months for proxy logs. We can export WORM snapshot but will need legal approval for extension.
ash: RBAC follow-up: don't widen service account entitlements. Instead we should implement short-lived JWT-scoped grants for custody:rotate that require an attestation signature and an approval token. That minimizes standing privileges.
maria: vuln triage note: if proxy failed-open (i.e., accepted mismatched fingerprint) during maintenance, that's a critical security bug. Confirmed logs show 403 not allow. But we should run a grep across last 90 days for any rewrap success events where fingerprint != record.
ops-oncall: running that sweep now  results ETA 30m.
qa: also ask customer to export their attestation artifact. If they can't provide it, that complicates proof-of-custody.
lucas: action items tracked:
1) ops-oncall: produce redacted proxy verification log + timeline bundle (ETA 6h)
2) maria: coordinate customer attestation upload and 1:1 compliance call (ETA 24h)
3) security: scope 90-day grep for fingerprint anomalies (ETA 4h)
4) infra/ash: draft short JIT entitlement design and add to backlog
ops-oncall: sweep done: no occurrences of mismatch-leading-to-allow in last 90 days. Only rejects found. attaching summary.
security-bot: :white_check_mark: Evidence bundle ticket created: EVID-2026-0402-01
maria: thanks team. once bundle is ready we'll schedule the compliance call and update the incident with final determination on responsibility. (thumbsup)
